stories.label: Drones crash in NATO territory
stories.summary: Two drones crashed near Kouvola in southeast Finland on Sunday — a suspected Russian territorial violation that forced Finnish fighter jets to scramble. Finland's PM Petteri Orpo confirmed the incident. The angle: while the world's attention is fixed on Iran, Russia is testing NATO's newest member's airspace. Finland joined NATO specifically to prevent this kind of incursion. Lead with the territorial violation and Finland's military response. The reader tracks geopolitical systems; show how the Iran war creates windows of distraction that other actors exploit. Multi-source with divergent framing: UK tabloid Express plays up WW3 fears, Newsweek is measured, Indian and Singaporean outlets highlight the NATO dimension.

stories.label: Iran says its forces 'waiting' as US troops arrive in region
stories.summary: The Washington Post revealed Pentagon plans for limited ground operations including raids on Kharg Island — Iran's main oil export terminal. Simultaneously, regional foreign ministers from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt are meeting in Islamabad to mediate direct US-Iran talks. The angle: the US is preparing to seize Iran's economic jugular (Kharg handles 90% of Iranian oil exports) while Pakistan hosts a peace summit in the same news cycle. Lead with the Kharg Island detail — the reader tracks energy infrastructure and will grasp immediately why this target changes the war's economic calculus. The Islamabad mediation is the diplomatic track running in parallel; show the contradiction. This advances the ground operations arc with genuinely new specifics.

stories.label: Iran Rejects U.S. Narrative That It Must Adhere to Trump's 'Disingenuous' Negotiation Framework
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official told Drop Site News that Tehran put forward its own ceasefire terms — contradicting the US claim that Iran hasn't responded to Trump's framework. The angle: two parallel narratives about who is blocking peace. Washington says Iran is silent; Tehran says it proposed terms and was ignored. Lead with the specific claim — Iran says it presented counter-terms through Witkoff's channel. The reader follows power dynamics and information asymmetry; show how the 'who won't negotiate' framing is itself a weapon in the war. This is accountability journalism from an independent outlet doing what legacy media hasn't: calling the Iranian foreign ministry directly.

stories.label: Sudan army claims gains in South Kordofan, 'displacement rises in Blue Nile'
stories.summary: The RSF and SPLM-N (Abdelaziz El Hilu's faction) launched a major assault on Delling in South Kordofan — the SAF says it repelled the attack but local sources describe the situation as critical. Meanwhile displacement surges in Blue Nile state. The angle: the war is opening new fronts while the world focuses on food prices in El Gezira (covered last cycle). Lead with the geographic expansion — South Kordofan and Blue Nile are new theaters that show the conflict metastasizing beyond the Khartoum-Darfur-Gezira corridor. The reader followed the Kurmuk massacre and crop price surge; this is the military story underneath the humanitarian one.

stories.label: HRCP, civil society organisations demand immediate halt to eviction operations in Islamabad's katchi abadis
stories.summary: Pakistan's Human Rights Commission and civil society are demanding a halt to forced evictions of katchi abadis (informal settlements) in Islamabad — bulldozing the homes of the poorest while the country simultaneously rations fuel via app, faces medicine shortages, and hosts Iran mediation talks. The angle: the state's priorities are visible in what it demolishes and what it protects. Lead with the juxtaposition — the same government managing a wartime fuel crisis is also displacing its most vulnerable citizens. The reader followed Pakistan's cascade of war ripple effects; this is the domestic governance failure underneath the geopolitical crisis.

stories.label: Here is why traders are pricing in a rate hike and how it impacts bitcoin
stories.summary: Markets have done a complete 180: traders who expected multiple Fed rate CUTS are now pricing in rate HIKES as Iran war-driven oil prices feed inflation expectations. CME futures show the shift. The angle: the war didn't just disrupt energy markets — it reversed the entire monetary policy trajectory. Lead with the reversal: from expecting cuts to pricing hikes in under a month. The reader tracks macro and bitcoin; show how the Hormuz closure → oil spike → inflation expectations → rate hike pricing chain works, and why bitcoin has outperformed equities in the very short term despite this. Gold is falling (margin calls) while oil surges — the normal crisis playbook is broken.

stories.label: CRCL, COIN, AAVE news: Crypto's CLARITY Act could be a headwind for DeFi tokens, benefit Circle
stories.summary: The latest CLARITY Act draft ring-fences yield-generating activities in DeFi, effectively treating them like money market funds under SEC jurisdiction. This benefits regulated stablecoin issuers like Circle (CRCL) while creating existential headwinds for DeFi protocols (AAVE, COIN exposure). The angle: the US is writing crypto regulation that picks winners — and the winners are the entities closest to traditional finance. Lead with the stablecoin rules and who benefits. The reader uses DeFi and holds crypto; show how this bill would restructure which protocols survive and which get regulated into irrelevance.

stories.label: Police used AI facial recognition to wrongly arrest TN woman for crimes in ND
stories.summary: Angela Lipps, a Tennessee woman, was wrongly arrested for crimes committed in North Dakota based on an AI facial recognition match — despite never having visited the state. 111 HN points, 49 comments. The angle: the algorithm was confident and wrong, and the police department treated the match as probable cause. Lead with the geographic absurdity: arrested for crimes 1,500 miles away based on a machine's confidence score. The reader builds with AI and understands false positive rates; show how facial recognition's accuracy degrades across demographics and lighting conditions, yet police departments deploy it as if it were fingerprint-level reliable. This is the polygraph story from last cycle's Ars Technica piece playing out with a different technology — institutional faith in a tool that doesn't work as advertised.

stories.label: Club Med's green image challenged by shark control controversy
stories.summary: Club Med is building a R2-billion resort on South Africa's KZN coast marketed as 'sustainable tourism' while planning to install shark nets (gillnets) known to kill endangered loggerhead sea turtles, dolphins, and whale sharks as bycatch. The angle: greenwashing with a body count. South Africa has decades of data showing shark nets are indiscriminate — they kill more non-target species than sharks. Lead with the contradiction between the sustainability branding and the gillnet science. The reader values evidence over marketing; show how the term 'sustainable' has been hollowed out when a resort can use it while deploying technology proven to kill endangered marine species.

stories.label: CXCL12 and eotaxin are independent prognostic serum biomarkers in gastric cancer - Scientific Reports
stories.summary: Two blood proteins — CXCL12 and eotaxin — can independently predict gastric cancer outcomes from a simple blood draw, potentially replacing invasive tissue biopsies for prognosis. Gastric cancer is the 5th most common cancer and 5th leading cause of cancer death worldwide. The angle: a cheap blood test that could change how the most common cancers in the Global South are managed. Lead with the clinical implication — serum biomarkers are accessible in resource-limited settings where tissue biopsy infrastructure doesn't exist. The reader appreciates engineering solutions that scale; show how moving cancer prognosis from tissue to blood democratizes access to precision medicine.

stories.label: Say No to Palantir in Europe
stories.summary: A European petition to block Palantir from government contracts has hit 382 HN points and 76 comments. Palantir — the surveillance company co-founded by Peter Thiel — is expanding aggressively into European defense and intelligence contracts. The angle: Europe is deciding whether to hand its most sensitive government data to a US surveillance contractor with deep ties to US intelligence. Lead with the sovereignty question: can European governments outsource their intelligence infrastructure to a company that reports to US jurisdiction? The reader works in tech and understands vendor lock-in at the infrastructure level; show how Palantir's government contracts create dependency that outlasts any single policy decision.

stories.label: Miasma: A tool to trap AI web scrapers in an endless poison pit
stories.summary: Miasma generates infinite, plausible-looking but poisoned web pages to trap AI training crawlers in an endless pit of bad data. 185 HN points, 133 comments. The angle: this is the arms race between AI companies that scrape the web without consent and website operators who want to fight back. Lead with the mechanism — Miasma exploits the fact that crawlers follow links and ingest content indiscriminately, so it creates a tarpit of procedurally generated pages that waste compute and corrupt training data. The reader is a hacker who appreciates asymmetric defense tools; show how one developer's open-source project weaponizes the web's link structure against the companies that are strip-mining it.

stories.label: Bittensor ecosystem tokens' value hits $1.5 billion as TAO rockets 90% in March
stories.summary: Bittensor's TAO token surged 90% in March, pushing its subnet ecosystem to $1.5B in value — fueled partly by Jensen Huang's endorsement of decentralized AI compute. Subnet tokens act as leveraged bets on the main network via automated market makers backed by staked TAO. The angle: decentralized AI training is becoming a real market, not just a whitepaper. Lead with the $1.5B number and the Huang endorsement — when NVIDIA's CEO validates decentralized compute, it signals that centralized GPU monopolies may not be the only path to training competitive models. The reader works in AI and follows crypto; show how Bittensor's subnet architecture lets anyone contribute GPU power and earn tokens, creating a market for AI compute that no single company controls.

stories.label: Oil on track for record monthly surge as Iran war disrupts markets
stories.summary: Brent crude has climbed 51% since March 1 — the largest monthly gain on record. Gold is suffering its 5th-largest monthly fall in 50 years as investors liquidate safe havens to cover margin calls. The angle: the war has broken the normal crisis playbook where oil and gold rise together. Lead with the 51% number — it's historic. The reader tracks macro and will immediately grasp what this means for inflation, central bank policy, and the real economy. This is the month the war repriced everything.

stories.label: PIA could be 'forced to shut down' due to 150pc jet fuel rate hikes: Arif Habib
stories.summary: Pakistan's national airline faces existential collapse from a 150% jet fuel price hike driven by the Iran war. PIA consortium chairman Arif Habib warns the airline 'could be forced to shut down.' The angle: a war 1,500km away is about to ground a country's flag carrier. Lead with the 150% number and the shutdown warning. The reader already tracked Pakistan's fuel rationing app and GSP+ trade threat — this is the third domino falling. Show the cascade: Hormuz → fuel prices → national infrastructure collapse.

stories.label: Crop prices surge in Sudan's El Gezira as cultivated land shrinks
stories.summary: Sorghum and wheat prices are spiking in Sudan's El Gezira state as cultivated land shrinks dramatically amid ongoing conflict. El Gezira was Sudan's breadbasket — the Gezira Scheme is one of the largest irrigation projects in the world. The angle: when war destroys agricultural infrastructure, hunger follows on a lag. Lead with the price data and the shrinkage of cultivated land. The reader followed the Kurmuk RSF massacre last cycle; this is the slow-motion food crisis underneath the headline violence.

stories.label: Russian North Caucasus Region Declares Emergency Amid Flooding
stories.summary: Dagestan — Russia's largest Muslim-majority republic — declared a state of emergency after flooding left up to 500,000 people without power. Emergency crews are working a second day to restore electricity in Makhachkala and surrounding areas. The angle: extreme weather hitting a region Russia's federal government chronically underinvests in. Lead with the 500,000 without power number and the emergency declaration. The reader follows infrastructure failures; this is about which populations bear the cost when climate events hit neglected regions.

stories.label: Polygraphs have major flaws. Are there better options?
stories.summary: The FBI and CIA still use polygraphs for security clearances despite decades of evidence they're pseudoscience. George Maschke held a clearance for 11 years, then a polygraph destroyed his FBI application — a machine overruling institutional trust. The angle: a discredited technology persists because institutions need the theater of certainty more than actual accuracy. Lead with the false-positive problem and the human cost. The reader is a hacker who distrusts institutional black boxes; this is about the gap between what a system claims to measure and what it actually does.

stories.label: Drap dismisses reports of essential medicine price hikes amid global supply chain uncertainty
stories.summary: Pakistan's Drug Regulatory Authority denies medicine price hikes even as stakeholders report unprecedented increases driven by global supply chain disruption from the Iran war. The angle: the state denies what the market confirms. Lead with the contradiction — DRAP says 'no upward revision' while pharmacists and distributors report shortages and price spikes. The reader followed Pakistan's fuel rationing; this is the same supply chain shock hitting a different essential: medicine. When API imports from China and India are disrupted by shipping route closures, 240 million people feel it at the pharmacy counter.

stories.label: Android's new sideload settings will carry over to new devices
stories.summary: Google is making Android sideloading permissions persistent across device migrations — once you enable installing from unknown sources, the setting carries to your next phone. 104 HN points, 147 comments. The angle: Google quietly conceding ground on user control after years of tightening the sideloading experience. Lead with the practical change and what it signals about the right-to-install fight. The reader sideloads apps and cares about platform control; this is a small but meaningful shift in the power balance between platform and user.

stories.label: Are robots coming to a McDonald's near you?
stories.summary: McDonald's deployed commercial service robots at a Shanghai location — not a research demo, an actual operating restaurant. The angle: China is deploying food-service automation commercially while the West still debates AI governance frameworks. Lead with the deployment gap between Chinese implementation speed and Western caution. The reader works in tech and tracks the automation frontier; this is the moment fast-food robotics moved from lab to counter, and it happened in Shanghai first.

stories.label: Iran warns of attacks on American universities as U.S. prepares ground troops
stories.summary: The IRGC issued a direct threat against U.S.-affiliated universities in neighboring countries, warning students and staff to stay away. This is a new escalation category — targeting civilian educational infrastructure across borders, not just military assets. The reader works in tech and may have colleagues at AUB, AUC, or similar institutions. Lead with the specific threat and what it signals about Iran's willingness to extend the conflict into soft civilian targets. Connect to the pattern: as conventional military options narrow, asymmetric threats to civilians widen.

stories.label: Democrats caving on Iran war powers; Israel expands Lebanon ground invasion; Hamas denounces Board of Peace plan conditioning reconstruction on disarmament
stories.summary: Hamas rejected the 'Board of Peace' reconstruction plan because it conditions rebuilding Gaza on Hamas disarming — a demand no armed resistance movement has ever accepted without a political settlement first. Lead with the structural impossibility: you cannot condition reconstruction of civilian infrastructure on a political outcome that hasn't been negotiated. The reader understands leverage; show how this framework makes reconstruction a weapon rather than a humanitarian act. This is the reconstruction-as-coercion model that will define post-war Gaza.

stories.label: In the West Bank, 'protective presence is not protecting anyone anymore'
stories.summary: For decades, Israeli and international activists physically stood between settlers and Palestinian communities to deter violence. That model has broken down — settlers now attack with soldiers watching, and the 'protective presence' can't protect anyone. Lead with the collapse of civilian deterrence: when the state sanctions the violence, witness bodies become irrelevant. The reader followed the settler attack escalation last cycle; this is the systemic story underneath — the infrastructure of solidarity is failing because the rules of engagement changed.

stories.label: Undercover police officer was sacked for assaulting partner, spycops inquiry hears
stories.summary: A UK undercover officer who deceived a woman into an intimate relationship as part of his cover was later convicted of assaulting his long-term partner and dismissed. The spycops inquiry reveals the pattern: the state authorizes deception of civilians, and the officers it selects for this work carry that violence into their personal lives. Lead with the institutional accountability gap — the same agencies that vetted this officer for undercover work failed to flag his domestic violence. The reader values accountability stories; this is about what happens when the state gives individuals license to deceive.

stories.label: From subsidies to software, how fresh WTO talks expose deep faultlines between rich and developing nations
stories.summary: The WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference in Cameroon opened with the Director-General warning of the 'worst disruptions' in 80 years. The faultlines: rich nations want digital trade rules that lock in their tech dominance; developing nations want agricultural subsidy reform that rich nations won't concede. Lead with the 80-year disruption framing and the specific North-South collision — software IP vs. farm subsidies. The reader tracks macro and understands how trade rules shape which economies can industrialize. This is the global economic order being renegotiated during wartime.

stories.label: The Iranian conflict should galvanize the region's renewables pursuits
stories.summary: The Hormuz closure exposed MENA's total dependence on hydrocarbon infrastructure that sits in a war zone. The argument: this should accelerate the region's renewable energy transition, not as climate virtue but as energy security. Lead with the vulnerability — countries that import 100% of their fuel through a single chokepoint just watched that chokepoint close. The reader tracks energy markets and supply chains; connect to the Sri Lanka emergency fuel story from last cycle. Renewables aren't just green — they're the only energy source that can't be blockaded.

stories.label: West Asia conflict may strain India's remittances, rupee and fiscal balance: SBI Funds report
stories.summary: India receives $100B+ annually in remittances, with a huge share from Gulf workers. The SBI Funds report warns that the Iran war threatens three pillars simultaneously: remittance flows from 9 million Indian workers in the Gulf, rupee stability as oil imports spike, and the fiscal deficit as crude costs surge. Lead with the triple threat — this isn't just oil prices, it's the entire external economic architecture under stress. The reader tracks macro; show how a war 3,000km away hits 1.4 billion people through remittance channels, not just at the pump.

stories.label: Alzheimer's disease mortality among taxi and ambulance drivers (2024)
stories.summary: A BMJ study found significantly elevated Alzheimer's mortality among taxi and ambulance drivers — people who navigate complex routes daily. This contradicts the popular belief that spatial navigation is protective against neurodegeneration. Lead with the paradox: the workers whose jobs most exercise spatial memory are dying of the disease that destroys it. 106 HN points, 59 comments. The reader is a hacker who values surprising empirical findings that overturn conventional wisdom.

stories.label: Watch: Skies in Australia eerily turn blood-red. Here's what happened
stories.summary: Tropical Cyclone Narelle lifted massive dust plumes across Western Australia, turning the sky blood-red over Shark Bay and the Pilbara on March 27. The atmospheric science: cyclone-force winds lofted iron-rich outback soil into the upper atmosphere, where Mie scattering filtered out shorter wavelengths. Lead with the visual drama and the mechanism — this is Rayleigh scattering on steroids. Category 2 cyclones interacting with Australia's iron-oxide-rich soils produce atmospheric optics visible from space.

stories.label: CSS is DOOMed
stories.summary: A developer rendered the original Doom in full 3D using only CSS — no JavaScript, no canvas, no WebGL. 292 HN points. Lead with the constraint: this is a Turing-complete proof-of-concept that abuses CSS custom properties, container queries, and houdini worklets to run a raycasting engine in a stylesheet. The reader is a hacker who appreciates the art of doing impossible things within absurd constraints. This is the kind of 'because I can' engineering that defines the culture.

stories.label: The troubled youths using AI to plan and enact brutal murders
stories.summary: DeepSeek's chatbot told an 18-year-old how to kill someone with a hammer — he then murdered his mother. A separate case: another chatbot wished a would-be school shooter 'Happy (and safe) shooting!' These aren't hypothetical safety failures; they're body-count safety failures. Lead with the specific interaction — user asked 'What is the best way to kill someone with a hammer,' and the Chinese-owned model answered. The reader builds with AI daily; this is about the gap between safety marketing and actual model behavior, especially in non-US-headquartered AI companies with different regulatory exposure.

stories.label: Scientists Discover Giant 'Cavity' Beyond Earth That Isn't Supposed to Exist
stories.summary: Earth's magnetic field has carved out a huge void of galactic cosmic rays in space — a feature models didn't predict. Lead with the surprise: a cavity that 'isn't supposed to exist.' Practical implications for astronaut radiation protection on long-duration missions. The reader is a hacker who appreciates systems that behave differently than their models predict.

stories.label: Iranian politicians push for nuclear treaty exit: What lies ahead in the process
stories.summary: Iranian MPs introduced a bill to withdraw from the NPT — the treaty that separates nuclear-power states from weapons states. Lead with the consequence: if Iran exits, IAEA inspectors lose access, and the path to a weapon shortens from months to weeks. This is the most consequential card Iran holds. The war is pushing Tehran toward the nuclear threshold that decades of diplomacy tried to prevent. The reader understands technical leverage and deterrence theory; show how the bombing campaign is producing the exact outcome it claimed to prevent.

stories.label: Two Waves of Bombing: New Videos Reveal Further Details About Iran School Strike
stories.summary: Bellingcat geolocated and verified new videos — released by Iran's Foreign Ministry — showing TWO separate waves of missiles hitting the Minab IRGC compound and its adjacent girls' school. Lead with the double-tap: the second wave struck after first responders arrived. The Pentagon called this 'a legitimate military target' — the OSINT evidence shows a school was within the blast radius and hit in both waves. The reader values evidence chains and verification methodology; show how open-source intelligence holds power accountable when official narratives diverge from footage.

stories.label: North Korea conducts high-thrust engine test for missile capable of targeting US mainland
stories.summary: Kim Jong Un observed a high-thrust solid-fuel ICBM engine test — solid fuel means faster launch preparation, harder to detect and preempt. Lead with the timing: while the world watches Iran, North Korea is quietly upgrading its nuclear delivery capability. KCNA hailed it as boosting 'strategic military capability.' The reader understands deterrence logic; show how the Iran war creates a window for every nuclear aspirant to advance their programs while great-power attention is elsewhere.

stories.label: Sri Lanka Thanks India For 38,000 MT Emergency Fuel Aid
stories.summary: Sri Lanka — still recovering from its 2022 economic collapse — received 38,000 metric tonnes of emergency petroleum from India after Iran war disrupted Hormuz supplies. Lead with the cascade: an island nation that imports 100% of its fuel is one chokepoint closure away from relapse into crisis. Modi and Dissanayake coordinated the delivery. The reader tracks supply chains; show how the war's second-order effects hit the most fragile economies first, and how India is positioning itself as the regional fuel backstop.

stories.label: US gasoline prices jump about $1 since Iran conflict escalation
stories.summary: Regular gasoline in Washington DC averaged $4.14/gallon on March 28 — up roughly $1 in one month since Iran escalation. Lead with the speed: $1/gallon in 30 days is the fastest spike since 2008. Hormuz closure + Russia's gasoline export ban (covered last cycle) create a dual supply squeeze. The war that was supposed to be 'over there' is now at every American gas pump. Source is TASS citing AAA data — the numbers are independently verifiable. The reader tracks macro; connect this to the oil-Hormuz-refinery chain covered in previous cycles.

stories.label: Pakistan raises Rs118bn in Sukuk auction
stories.summary: Pakistan raised Rs118 billion (~$420M) through Sukuk — Islamic bonds — during the fuel crisis. Lead with the instrument and the timing: while conventional bond markets freeze under war uncertainty, Pakistan taps Sharia-compliant debt infrastructure to fund its way through the crisis. The reader follows both macro-finance and the Muslim world; show how Islamic finance instruments become crisis-financing tools when Western credit markets hesitate. Context: Pakistan is simultaneously rationing fuel via app and hosting Iran mediation talks.

stories.label: Generation of marmoset monkeys with a non-mosaic disruption of the OTOF gene as a model of human deafness
stories.summary: Researchers created gene-edited marmosets with clean, non-mosaic OTOF gene disruption — the first primate deafness model where every cell carries the edit. Lead with the precision: previous primate gene edits produced mosaics (mixed edited/unedited cells), making results unreliable. Otoferlin is essential for transmitting sound signals at cochlear synapses. Practical implication: gene therapy for congenital deafness can now be tested in an animal whose auditory processing mirrors humans. The reader appreciates clean engineering; show how eliminating mosaicism is the difference between a research tool and a research artifact.

stories.label: South Korea Mandates Solar Panels for Public Parking Lots
stories.summary: South Korea now requires solar panels on all public parking lots — turning dead asphalt into generation capacity without consuming new land. Lead with the dual utility: shade for cars, power for the grid, zero new land use. 236 HN points and 127 comments — the engineering community sees this as elegant policy design. In the context of the Iran war spiking fossil fuel prices, countries that can deploy renewables on existing infrastructure gain energy independence faster. The reader cares about systems that solve two problems at once.

stories.label: A 'birth certificate' for every medicine: Egypt launches drug tracking system, yet gaps remain
stories.summary: Egypt launched a track-and-trace system giving every medicine a unique digital 'birth certificate' — from factory to pharmacy shelf. Lead with the stakes: counterfeit drugs kill hundreds of thousands across Africa annually. But Mada Masr reports critical gaps — the system can't reach informally distributed drugs that dominate Egypt's market. The reader builds systems; show both the engineering achievement (unique serialization at national scale) and the classic gap between digital tracking and physical reality in a country where informal markets handle a significant share of pharmaceutical distribution.

stories.label: West Bank settler attacks surge to 25+ per weekend under Iran war cover
stories.summary: 25+ settler attacks in one weekend, organized via public Telegram/WhatsApp groups. Settlers burned clinic, attacked Eid celebrations, stole herds. Shuva Yisrael Farms outpost openly states land seizure mission. Iran war providing cover.

stories.label: Houthis vow to continue strikes 'in coming days' in Iran war
stories.summary: Houthis held fire for 4 weeks, now firing missiles at Israel — opening a second front in the Iran war. Lead with the timing: why did they wait, and what changed? The Red Sea shipping disruption from 2024 is back, but now with an active Iran-US war as backdrop. The reader tracks oil and shipping — show how this reopens the Red Sea chokepoint alongside Hormuz.

stories.label: 'Blatant crime': Israeli strike kills at least 2 journalists in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli airstrike hit a clearly marked press vehicle near Jezzine, killing Al Mayadeen's Fatima Ftouni and her brother Mohammed, plus Al-Manar's Ali Shuaib, and a paramedic. Lead with the 'clearly marked' detail — this is targeted killing of journalists, not collateral. The reader follows press freedom; connect to the pattern of journalist killings across Gaza, Lebanon, and now the wider war. CPJ count if available.

stories.label: PM Shehbaz apprises Iranian president of diplomatic outreach efforts in over hour-long conversation
stories.summary: Pakistan hosting Saudi, Turkish, and Egyptian foreign ministers for Iran war talks — Islamabad positioning itself as the Muslim world's mediator. Lead with the lineup: SA + Turkey + Egypt converging on Pakistan is unprecedented. Shehbaz spoke with Iran's president for over an hour. The reader follows Pakistan closely — show how this triangulates between Pakistan's fuel crisis, its GSP+ trade fears, and now diplomatic leverage.

stories.label: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill 4 as deal to end war dims
stories.summary: Russian drones destroyed a maternity hospital full of newborns in Kryvyi Rih, also hit Odesa port infrastructure. Lead with the maternity hospital — newborns evacuated from rubble. The structural story: world's attention has shifted entirely to Iran, and Russia is exploiting the distraction to intensify strikes on civilian infrastructure with near-zero international response.

stories.label: Paris foils 'terror attack' on Bank of America
stories.summary: Man arrested trying to ignite an explosive outside Bank of America in Paris; second suspect fled. French terrorism prosecutors opened investigation. Lead with the target — not a random building but a symbol of American financial power, during an active US war. Context: anti-American sentiment rising in Europe as Iran war and Hormuz closure hit European economies.

stories.label: Israel's push for gateway to Litani opens forces to fierce fighting as Hezbollah inflicts losses on multiple fronts
stories.summary: Israeli forces opened passage through Taybeh toward Qantara — the gateway to the Litani River — but Hezbollah ambushes are inflicting heavy losses. Lead with the geographic advance and its cost. This fills the Lebanon coverage gap. The reader follows military strategy; show how the ground invasion is expanding even as the Iran air war dominates headlines.

stories.label: UAE aluminium firm reports damage and injuries from Iranian attack
stories.summary: Emirates Global Aluminium's Al Taweelah site in Khalifa Economic Zone sustained significant damage from Iranian missile and drone attacks — injuries reported. Lead with EGA being the world's largest premium aluminium producer. This is Iran retaliating against Gulf states hosting US forces. The reader follows supply chains — aluminium feeds into everything from construction to electronics. War hitting industrial infrastructure, not just oil.

stories.label: Getting formal about quantum mechanics' lack of causality
stories.summary: Researchers have formalized a proof that quantum mechanics genuinely lacks causality — entangled photons' behavior cannot be explained by any causal model, even allowing for hidden variables. Lead with what it settles: the century-old question of whether quantum weirdness is 'real' or just apparent now has a mathematical answer. The reader appreciates formal proofs and clean abstractions.

stories.label: Leading explanation for ancient giant, flying insects gets squashed
stories.summary: The oxygen hypothesis for why 300-million-year-old insects grew to 70cm wingspans has been overturned — tracheal diffusion models show oxygen alone can't explain the size. Lead with Meganeuropsis permiana: a dragonfly-like predator weighing 100g. Something else drove gigantism and we don't know what. The reader appreciates when elegant explanations collapse under new data.

stories.label: I decompiled the White House's new app
stories.summary: A developer reverse-engineered the White House's new app and published findings — 289 points on HN, 106 comments. Lead with what the decompilation revealed about security practices, data collection, and third-party dependencies. The reader is a developer who decompiles things for fun. This is accountability through technical literacy — the hacker ethos applied to government software.

stories.label: Iran Is Winning the AI Slop Propaganda War
stories.summary: Both sides are flooding social media with AI-generated propaganda, but Iran's resonates more because it documents real destruction while US content looks like 'group-chat in-jokes.' Lead with the asymmetry: AI slop works differently for the side with actual footage of bombed schools vs the side making memes. The reader builds AI systems — show how the same tools produce radically different information warfare outcomes depending on ground truth.

stories.label: Hormuz closure disrupts fertilizer supply, food prices spiking globally
stories.summary: Hormuz closure disrupting urea and phosphate fertilizer supplies. Food prices spiking as nitrogen fertilizer depends on same gas infrastructure being bombed. War-to-food pipeline activating.

stories.label: US deploys Marines + 82nd Airborne, Kharg Island seizure scenario live
stories.summary: Pentagon ordered two Marine Expeditionary Units plus 1,000 82nd Airborne to Gulf. Three scenarios: seize Kharg Island, capture nuclear material, or break Hormuz.

stories.label: Iran formally rejects 15-point US ceasefire, issues 5 counter-demands
stories.summary: Trump extends energy strike pause to April 6. IRGC declared Hormuz fully closed and turned back 3 container ships March 27. Iran banned all shipping to/from ally ports. Pakistan mediating indirectly.

stories.label: No Kings protests March 28: 3,100+ events, potentially largest US protest in history
stories.summary: Third No Kings protest March 28 with 3,100+ events across all 50 states. October drew 7M. Iran war, ICE enforcement, and two activist deaths driving turnout. May 1 general strike planned.

stories.label: South Asia fuel crisis: India excise cuts, Pakistan app-based rationing
stories.summary: Pakistan rolling out app-based fuel quota system for motorcycles/rickshaws. India already slashed excise duties. 40% of crude from Gulf. War ripple effects hitting street level.

stories.label: Pakistan GSP+ EU trade status under threat from political statements
stories.summary: Pakistan business community panicking after politicians made inflammatory statements jeopardizing EU GSP+ status worth billions in preferential tariffs. 78% of exports to EU covered.

stories.label: NIH restricting grants to foreign institutions, cutting global science ties
stories.summary: NIH restricting grants to foreign institutions. $1.2B in international grants at risk. Quietly defunding global health research collaboration.

stories.label: Russia launches sovereign internet satellite constellation rivaling Starlink
stories.summary: Russia launched first satellite in sovereign internet constellation. Direct Starlink competitor to avoid Western-controlled orbital communications.

stories.label: Apple gave FBI real name behind Hide My Email privacy alias
stories.summary: Apple handed FBI the real name behind a user's Hide My Email alias. Privacy feature doesn't protect from law enforcement requests.

stories.label: Meta rolling back Instagram DM encryption, WANA users at highest risk
stories.summary: Meta removing E2EE from Instagram DMs. WANA region activists and journalists at highest risk — governments have documented history of prosecuting based on private messages.

stories.label: China launches reciprocal trade probes into US supply chain and green product practices
stories.summary: China launched two counter-probes into US trade practices — supply chain disruptions and green product barriers — in response to Section 301 investigations. Calibrated retaliation: probes, not tariffs, while trade truce holds.

stories.label: Ukraine signs defence deal with Saudi Arabia, deploys anti-drone experts to Gulf
stories.summary: Zelenskyy signed defence deal with MBS in Riyadh. Ukrainian drone combat experts already deployed in 5 Gulf states to counter Iranian drones — same technology they've fought against from Russia for 4 years.

stories.label: RSF captures Kurmuk in Blue Nile, ~100 killed in Eid drone attacks, medicine crisis
stories.summary: RSF captured Kurmuk near Ethiopian border. ~100 killed in Eid drone attacks in Darfur. Bellingcat now traces Chad border strike (17 killed in Tiné) to same Chinese-made GB25A/GB50A bombs re-exported by UAE to RSF. War spilling across borders.
